start[n..] instead of start[n + 1..] unreserves the job that failed a second time, right after the first: unreserving is the same done twice
a machine never seen running, swept at exactly ten minutes to the millisecond or one millisecond later: no test can hold a sweep to that millisecond without the sweep's GitHub checks deciding first

a further GitLab is shown when the control plane lists its id at its address; with || it would be taken as shown when another connection had the same address, which a control plane that keeps one connection per id never lists alongside a new one it dropped
the dashboard's views read again at every look instead of being kept a moment: the same pages, only more reads
the default for a key never asked for: u64::MAX / KEY_WAIT_MS is still tens of thousands of years from now, as u64::MAX - KEY_WAIT_MS is: never waited out either way

the test kit's wait for a Worker to answer, after wrangler said it is ready: taken as answering at once, a test's first request waits while the Worker's module loads instead (too long only on a busy machine, which is what the wait is for)

killed by only_the_worker_says_what_its_settings_and_keys_are (a long bearer that is no key, beside a key that holds, is refused), but the mutation run tests the Worker built before it, so no mutant of the Worker reaches that test

whether a test may skip for want of Chrome, Node or the built Worker: Coverage and its mutants set SUPERCI_NO_SKIPS and have all three, so taken as never skipping changes nothing there (what_a_test_needs_and_is_not_here_fails_a_run_that_skips_nothing holds it to the variable where it is unset)
